title: cost-holster-prefill-optimizer-and-quant-guidance
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Customers with bursty, cold-start workloads pay disproportionately for first tokens when KV caches and warmups miss. This PR introduces the "cost-holster" prefill optimizer: a lightweight service + config model that recommends tenant-scoped prefill/warmup templates and quantization guidance based on traces and unit-econ signals. Motivation: instead of one-size-fits-all defaults, we can reduce per-token cost for cold paths by combining short targeted warmups, smarter prefill sizes, and safe quantization hints.

What this PR contains (single-line description): implement prefill analysis pipeline, tenant profile exporter, guidance engine, telemetry hooks, and a safe rollout path behind feature flag.

Key changes and rationale:
- Introduced packages/prefill/engine: analysis + candidate generator that consumes sampled traces and outputs ranked prefill templates (short warmups, padding heuristics, kv-prefetch toggles). Rationale: keep decision logic close to prefill lifecycle and make it pluggable for future heuristics.
- Added cmd/prefill-advisor CLI to export tenant recommendations for manual review and to drive opt-in experiments.
- Extended telemetry: added metrics (prefill_recommendation_count, estimated_tokens_saved, simulated_cost_delta_usd) and spans for the analysis pipeline to the observability-pack. These let ops validate unit economic impact before rollout.
- Quant guidance component: light-weight rule engine that suggests quant profiles (int8/4bit, per-model guidance) when simulated sample-quality regression < 0.6% based on our eval harness. This is intentionally conservative and outputs a 'suggestion' not enforced change.
- API and config: new TenantPrefillConfig CRD-like JSON blob in tenant defaults; console integration planned in follow-up. Defaults preserved; all behavior behind feature flag: PREFILL_COST_HOLSTER_ENABLED=false by default.

Checklist:
- [x] Analysis algorithm + sampling pipeline implemented
- [x] Telemetry and simulation metrics emitted
- [x] CLI for export and dry-run implemented
- [x] Unit and integration tests added for engine heuristics and quant-safeguard checker
- [x] Feature flag gating and migration path documented

Performance and unit-econ summary (local sim):
- On a 10k-request sample from a mid-market customer: estimated median token-cost reduction 11.6% (simulated), p95 cost reduction 6.2% (conservative tail).
- Average added latency for cold requests (prefill synth) +12ms median, +40ms p95 for items that run the warmup sampler; most requests unaffected.
- Quant guidance projected to reduce token compute cost an additional ~3-5% in safe cohorts (when suggested and manually enabled).

Commits summary: commit messages are included below.

Files touched (high level):
- packages/prefill/engine/analysis.go - core heuristic pipeline and candidate ranking
- packages/prefill/engine/simulate.go - lightweight simulator for cost delta estimation
- cmd/prefill-advisor/main.go - CLI to export suggestions as JSONL for review
- observability-pack/metrics/prefill_metrics.go - new metrics and tagging
- eval-harness/prefill_quality/test_profiles.yaml - new test profiles for quality regression checks
- internal/config/defaults/prefill_defaults.json - tenant config schema and example presets
- web/console-api/handlers/prefill_suggestions.go - API endpoint (guarded, feature-flagged)
- tests/prefill/engine_test.go - unit + integration tests
- docker/prefill/Dockerfile - small runtime image for the CLI and dry-run jobs
- docs/ops/prefill_cost_holster.md - rollout and runbook

Review notes and conversation (chronological):
- Jonah Kim: "Can we avoid any automatic enforcement? I want suggestions to be manual for the first two months."
  - Aisha: "Agreed — suggestions only. All enforcement toggles require explicit tenant opt-in or an enable flag per-tenant. Documented in ops runbook."
- Leila Ortiz: "Simulator needs more guardrails around sample bias; drop samples with fewer than 200 trace points."
  - Aisha: "Added a prefilter (see analysis.go) and added an integration test that fails fast on low-sample inputs."
- Marcus Nguyen: "CI flaked on linting — please run new lint rules and pin module versions."
  - Aisha: "Fixed lint errors, pinned dependency patches in go.mod; CI green on rerun."
- Performance reviewer (automated): "Telemetry lacks a cardinality policy for tenant id tags."
  - Aisha: "Updated metrics to use tenant cohort tags (low cardinality) and added sampling to spans in observability-pack."

CI summary: initial CI run: fail (lint + one flaky integration test), second run: pass. E2E smoke included: prefill-advisor dry-run against recording dataset.

Testing and validation performed:
- Unit tests for ranking/heuristics (packages/prefill/engine)
- Integration test with simulated KV cache hits/misses and cost simulator
- Manual dry-run on three tenants (dev-staging, canary-1, canary-2) with exported JSONL reviewed by SRE and Data Science
- Telemetry validation: simulated_cost_delta_usd and estimated_tokens_saved validated against recorded billing traces in canary tenants

Rollout plan and safety:
1) Merge behind feature flag (this PR).
2) Deploy to staging; run prefill-advisor CLI with recorded traces to generate suggestions and surface them to SRE/DS for QA (1 week).
3) Enable suggestions in canary tenants (opt-in); monitor simulated_cost_delta_usd and real billing signal (2 weeks).
4) If signals match simulation and quality regressions < 0.6% on evaluation suite, enable console UI to let tenants opt into auto-apply (manual opt-in by tenant).
5) Consider rolling out auto-apply only after 90 days of stable telemetry and per-tenant audits.

Backward compatibility: No breaking changes by default; config additions are additive. breaking_change=false.

Notes for reviewers: focus on analysis.go heuristics, the simulator's cost model assumptions (simulate.go), and telemetry cardinality. The quant guidance rules are intentionally conservative — please validate eval-harness profiles.

Release notes: "Introduce Cost Holster: a prefill recommendation engine that suggests warmup and quantization guidance to reduce cold-path unit economics. Suggestions are opt-in and gated by feature flag. Adds telemetry for simulated savings and a CLI for dry-run exports."
